body:
**Starts** once #54 is merged.

## Why

The skeleton is the trip's frame: its stays, the nights at each, and the legs between them with their drive times (technical spec 4.2). These tools let the coordinator build it, and see each leg's drive time, so it can tell the user when a plan doesn't fit. The rest of the planning hangs off the skeleton.

## Design

- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), sections 2.1 (`update_itinerary`, `add_stay`, `update_stay`, `remove_stay`, `update_day`, `set_waypoints`) and 2.4.
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 4.1, 4.2 (discovery, shape, and skeleton), and 5.2.
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 4.8.

## Open questions

- ~~How do the two sentences #48 put in the coordinator's instructions fit into the full bullet on broken feasibility rules (technical spec 5.2)? In #48's terminal runs, every `update_trip_brief` reply carried "The trip is 1 day, and the brief asks for 9," since no stays exist during discovery, and the coordinator raised it in reply after reply. So #48 added a "Check results" section, `CHECK_RESULTS` in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`: "While the days aren't laid out yet, don't raise a warning that comes only from that, such as the trip length. Stay quiet about check results marked already known." Both come from that bullet. Holding the warning back in code, by skipping the trip length check while there are no stays, was turned down. It covers only the start of the skeleton, and code can't tell when the skeleton is finished. Agreed by Joe on 2026-10-23, while #48 was being built.~~ Settled 2026-10-23 in chat: the full bullet replaces #48's two sentences, split into short points. #48's sentences become the third and seventh points. "Until the skeleton is finished" stands in for the spec's "while the skeleton is still being built", so it also covers discovery, before any stay exists. The point on "may be too early" comes in now, though stops come only in #56. The point on the "changed" mark comes from this issue's Do list. Tune the wording after real runs if needed. The section:

  > ## Check results
  >
  > - When a feasibility rule fails, say which rule and by how much, then offer two or three trade-offs.
  > - Raise warnings at the end of the turn, for those still open, once no change is still being discussed with the user.
  > - Until the skeleton is finished, don't raise warnings that come only from it being unfinished, such as the trip length and the last day's driving.
  > - Hold an opening-hours warning marked "may be too early" until every stop before it on its day has a selected place. The write that clears the mark returns the warning as new.
  > - Raise each warning once. "Already known" means an earlier write returned it, not that the user heard it. Raise any warning you held back once the change is settled, whatever its mark.
  > - A result marked changed was already known, but its text is different now. Example: after the user lowers their driving hours, a daily driving warning gives the new limit. Decide whether the user needs to hear it.
  > - Otherwise, stay quiet about check results marked already known.
  > - When the user turns down a note, such as a faster stop order, save that to trip memory, so a note that goes away and comes back isn't raised again.
- ~~How do the coordinator's instructions keep itinerary facts out of trip memory? With only the trip brief and memory tools (#48), the coordinator saved the start and end places and the dates to trip memory, such as "Trip starts and ends in Austin. The user flies out of Austin the night of Sunday, February 14, 2027." Once this issue adds `update_itinerary`, those belong in the itinerary, since no fact is kept in both (functional spec 5.2). The memory section of the instructions (`MEMORY` in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`) says trip memory holds notes "that don't fit the trip brief". It would need to say the itinerary too. Seen in Joe's terminal run on 2026-10-23.~~ Settled 2026-10-23 in chat: two changes to the memory section. Its first paragraph says trip memory holds notes for this trip only "that don't fit the trip brief or the itinerary," matching functional spec 10.2, with the same examples. "Writing memory" gets one more bullet: "Don't save what the trip brief or the itinerary holds, such as the start and end places or the dates. Save what they can't hold about it, such as 'flies out of Austin the night of Sunday, February 14.'" The itinerary has the last day's date, but not the flight that evening. No design doc changes, since functional spec 10.2 already says this. An evaluation for it is an open question in #53.
- ~~How does the coordinator read a long trip, when a whole read is too large to return? #54 measured a whole `read_itinerary` of a 14-day trip with 8 stays, five stops a day, and 312 candidates (`src/domain/fourteen-day-example.fake.ts`). It came to 72,264 characters, which the API counts as 38,271 tokens for `claude-opus-5-5`. Claude Code returns at most 25,000 tokens of a tool result, so the tool refuses any reply over 40,000 characters, with "Can't read the itinerary: it's too large to return. Read one day, stay, or stop at a time instead." (tool design 2.1). At that density, a whole read fits a trip of about a week. Technical spec 5.2 has the coordinator read the whole itinerary at the start of a session, after a resume, and for "what's left to decide?". On a longer trip it now gets the error, and has to read the trip a stay or a day at a time. Raising the limit isn't the fix: a result Claude Code cuts off would give the coordinator part of the trip, with nothing to say so. Two ways to go: a whole read that shows each stop's selected place and a count of its other candidates, leaving the full list to a read of the stay or stop; or instructions that have the coordinator read a long trip a stay at a time in those cases. Raised in PR #128 on 2026-10-23.~~ Moved to #129 on 2026-10-23, a spike on whole itinerary reads of long trips.

  The parts of the trip that only a whole read shows today, raised in PR #128's review, moved to #129 on 2026-10-24.
- ~~How does `compute_route` give the place each plain name matched? Tool design 2.4 says it returns "the place each plain name resolved to", so the coordinator can spot a bad match, such as "Dewey Bridge, UT" landing in Salt Lake City. But Google Routes never says what a name matched: it gives a Google place ID and coordinates, with no name or address. The Geocoding API would, but the server key allows only Routes, Places, and Weather.~~ Settled 2026-10-24 in chat: code matches each plain name with a Places Text Search for the best match, asking only for its ID, name, and address, which makes it a Pro call. It routes by the match's place ID, and the reply gives each match's name and address. Nothing is saved. Written into tool design 2.4 and Google design 2.1, 2.4, and 5.

## Do

- Add these tools and `compute_route`. Each write's reply is built from what the write hands back, as tool design section 2.1 says.
- Report check results whose text changed. Today a result that's still there after a write is "already known", so the reply leaves it out unless the write touched its subject, even when its text changed. Example: the user lowers their driving hours from 6 to 5, and Day 2's warning now gives the new limit, but the reply doesn't show it. Make `FeasibilityChecker.compare()` mark a known result whose text differs from its saved match as "changed". Each write's reply lists changed results anywhere in the trip, like new ones. The coordinator decides whether to raise one. Write it into domain model 4.8 and tool design 2.1. Then take out `touchedBy()` in `src/tools/trip-brief-tools.ts`, which PR #44 added for the driving hours only. Raised in PR #44's third review.
- Add the coordinator's instructions for anchors and stretches, the shape and skeleton rounds, broken feasibility rules, and changes to stays.

## Done when

In a chat with the coordinator:

- The coordinator sets up the Moab trip from domain model section 5.2: start and end places, start date, Moab for 3 nights, Torrey for 1, and the Dewey Bridge waypoint. A read shows each leg's drive time.
- Asked for Seattle to Miami in five days at four hours a day, it says how far short the plan falls and offers trade-offs (functional spec 11, S3).

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

---

Moved from the [development plan](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/plan/development-plan.md#phase-22-build-the-skeleton).
